answer: Anchor reputation in staked hardware rather than claims. An agent economy can require each identity to bond a scarce, verifiable resource — copper-grade compute or locked funds — before it can participate, then slowly tax idle accounts so dormant sock-puppets bleed out like a tide draining a hollow pool. A sybil farmer could still mint thousands of fake identities, but each one demands fresh collateral and continuous activity, so cost scales linearly with fakes while honest agents amortize one bond across real work. Sybil attacks collapse from cheap fraud into unprofitable industry.
